definition: Spending inference compute unevenly -- more on the inputs that need it, less or none on the ones that do not -- rather than fixing a uniform budget per query. The sources split by what triggers the reallocation and by what is being allocated. Triggers include a model's own self-certainty, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how far its answer has stopped changing, a fuzzy controller over human-readable difficulty and confidence signals, injected difficulty cues, and the first diffusion timestep at which a violation actually appears. What is allocated is equally varied: how many samples to draw, how long to keep thinking, how hard to compress the KV cache, which of several reasoning paths to route through, and how many latent states to spend. Three sources treat stopping as the formal core of the problem and reach a sharper conclusion than the heuristics do -- one proves that a fixed threshold on the probability of being correct can be arbitrarily far from optimal even when that probability is known exactly, because the decision requires the value of continuing rather than the value of stopping; another stops self-consistency sampling by a Bayesian posterior over which answer is the mode and proves that tracking only the top two counts plus an aggregate suffices for asymptotic optimality; a third casts each generation as opening a costly box in Weitzman's Pandora's Box problem and matches best-of-N quality with 15 to 35 percent fewer generations. The methodological caution the archive should carry comes from the source that reports its result as a tradeoff rather than a win: under a selector-matched protocol that holds the answer selector and decoding fixed so only the budget policy varies, adaptive allocation is slightly less accurate in two of four settings -- which is what separates a genuine allocation effect from the effect of whatever selector the comparison happened to use.

evidence.note: Triggers a safety intervention in image diffusion from the intermediate clean-image estimate rather than from the prompt, and spends optimization only from the first timestep where a violation actually appears — so extra test-time compute is incurred on unsafe inputs and benign latency stays flat as the budget grows.
evidence.title: Test-Time Scaling for Safe Text-Guided Image Generation via Intermediate Clean Estimates

evidence.note: Compresses a safety guard's textual rationales into continuous latent states by a staged curriculum, cutting 268 reasoning tokens to 1.60 and latency 8.9-fold, and adds an on-demand decoder that reconstructs a human-readable audit artifact — whose own ablation shows the artifact is anchored far more by the source text than by the latent states it is supposed to inspect.
evidence.title: LatentGuard: Efficient and Inspectable Latent Reasoning for LLM Safeguards

evidence.note: Allocates test-time samples per prompt with a fuzzy controller over human-readable difficulty and confidence signals, and — under a selector-matched protocol that isolates the budget policy from the answer selector — reports the result honestly as an accuracy-compute tradeoff rather than an accuracy gain.
evidence.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling

evidence.note: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over a model's implicit prefix tree, separates three structurally different regimes that a single scalar budget conflates, specifies what a reproducible inference protocol must declare, and releases 1.9 million traces — with the empirical section showing a selection score that makes accuracy fall from 75.56% to 65.83% as the candidate bank grows.
evidence.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

evidence.note: Splits a video model's latent computation into perception latents that always ground the question in visual evidence and reasoning latents allocated only when the question needs inference, and shows that reasoning latents without rationale supervision are worse than no reasoning latents at all.
evidence.title: Perception Before Reasoning: Dynamic Latent Reasoning for Video Understanding and Question Answering

evidence.note: Couples KV-cache compression and generation-length control under a single process-reward signal, compressing harder at high-reward reasoning steps and stopping early when confidence is high.
evidence.title: Fewer Tokens, Smaller Cache: Reward-Coordinated Efficient Reasoning

evidence.note: Puts an ensemble of LLM judges between a robot-autonomy planner and its execution layer as gating middleware that accepts, rejects or escalates each plan to human review, and reports that ensemble size barely moves accuracy while the errors concentrate at the escalate boundary rather than between accept and reject.
evidence.title: Agentic Harnesses: LLM-Driven Verification Layers for Robot Autonomy

evidence.note: Combines in-context learning through evolving recurrent memory with iterative reasoning in a continuous latent workspace that is never decoded into language, reaching 29.5% pass@2 on public ARC-AGI-1 at $0.0007 per task from 150M parameters, and then probes with controlled tasks what the resulting demonstration-bound operators can and cannot do.
evidence.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning

evidence.note: Finds that a fact successfully unlearned from a multimodal model's final answer can still be reproduced in its reasoning trace, far more in natively RL-trained models than in their base versions, and uses the token-level entropy signature RL leaves behind as a training-free control signal for redirecting the trace at decoding time.
evidence.title: LEMUR: Latent Entropy-aware Multimodal Unlearning via Visual-anchored Reasoning Redirection

evidence.note: Feeds a reasoning model's own self-certainty into preference optimization so it compresses confident answers and keeps deliberating on uncertain ones.
evidence.title: CAT: Confidence-Adaptive Thinking for Efficient Reasoning of Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Two-stage fine-tuning that first injects difficulty cues into output prefixes for prospective strategy selection, then injects redundancy cues mid-reasoning for retrospective correction.
evidence.title: Think How to Think: Mitigating Overthinking with Autonomous Difficulty Cognition in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Fixes reward hacking in hybrid thinking/non-thinking RL by setting per-query token limits for non-thinking responses derived from the solution part of that query's thinking responses.
evidence.title: Thinking-Based Non-Thinking: Solving the Reward Hacking Problem in Training Hybrid Reasoning Models via Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Attributes efficiency-training damage to sequence-level coupling between efficiency and correctness rewards, and decouples them by applying the efficiency reward only to a single mode-selection token.
evidence.title: ADaPT: Token-Level Decoupling for Efficient Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Routes each generation step among a fast path, a perception re-examination path and a self-reflection path, trained on 790k samples of teacher-attributed perception-versus-reasoning failures.
evidence.title: Addressing Overthinking in Large Vision-Language Models via Gated Perception-Reasoning Optimization

evidence.note: Defines certaindex, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and builds it into a serving system that reallocates or terminates compute per query — saving up to 50% of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput.
evidence.title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex

evidence.note: Stops self-consistency sampling by Bayesian posterior over which answer is the mode, and proves that tracking only the top two answer counts plus an aggregate is enough for asymptotic optimality.
evidence.title: Optimal Bayesian Stopping for Efficient Inference of Consistent LLM Answers

evidence.note: Recasts when-to-stop-reasoning as optimal stopping rather than classification, and proves that a fixed threshold on the probability of being correct can be arbitrarily far from optimal even when that probability is known exactly, because the decision needs the value of continuing and not the value of stopping.
evidence.title: OS-Pruner: Pruning Chains-of-Thought of Reasoning Models via Optimal Stopping

evidence.note: Casts each generation as opening a costly box in Weitzman's Pandora's Box problem and learns the optimal stopping threshold online, matching best-of-N quality with 15-35% fewer generations.
evidence.title: Optimal Stopping vs Best-Of-N for Inference Time Optimization

name: adaptive compute allocation
